matches.rationale: GT 1 concerns missing statistical significance measures (standard deviations, confidence intervals) for Table 1 FID results. Finding 2 identifies numerical inconsistencies between Table 1 and Table 9 values, which is a different issue about data integrity across tables rather than lack of uncertainty quantification.

Both identify the same contradiction in Equation 9: GT 2 notes the summation over N conflicts with the text stating alignment at specific single layers (n=4 or n=8). Finding 5 identifies the identical issue—the summation index n collides with the layer index, creating an internally inconsistent loss definition.

GT 3 flags the Abstract's claim that 'SiT-L/2 + REG trained for 400K iterations outperforms SiT-XL/2 + REPA trained for 4M iterations' as oversimplified. Finding 4 identifies a direct contradiction where the Introduction attributes this achievement to REPA instead of REG, revealing the same underlying claim inconsistency issue.

GT 4 concerns the absence of variability measures (standard deviations, multiple runs) throughout the Experiments section. None of the findings address this missing uncertainty quantification; Finding 2 and 3 concern numerical inconsistencies, not missing statistical protocols.

GT 5 identifies rhetorical manipulation through superlatives like '63× faster' and 'surpasses' without caveats in the Introduction. None of the findings address presentation tone or rhetorical framing; they focus on technical errors and data inconsistencies.

GT 6 concerns the omission of ethical considerations, IRB statements, and bias discussion in the Appendix/Conclusion. None of the findings address ethical integrity or responsible research practices; all focus on technical and data issues.

GT 7 identifies that Table 16 shows REG underperforming REPA at early epochs (1.86 vs 1.42 at 80 epochs) contradicting claims of superior convergence. None of the findings examine Table 16 or early-stage training dynamics; Finding 2 and 3 concern different tables and metrics.

GT 8 concerns insufficient guidance on hyperparameters β and λ in Section 3.2, undermining reproducibility. None of the findings address hyperparameter tuning, sensitivity analysis, or reproducibility protocols; Finding 5 concerns equation inconsistency, not parameter guidance.

GT 9 identifies REPA-E [21] as a potentially fabricated or non-existent reference in Related Work. None of the findings examine reference validity or citation integrity; all focus on internal technical and data consistency issues.

GT 10 flags Table 6 showing unexpectedly large FID improvement (33.0 to 26.67) from entanglement alone without alignment. Finding 3 identifies the same table and notes the actual improvement is 29.9 (9.4% reduction), revealing inconsistency between text claims and table data for the same experimental result.

GT 11 concerns overgeneralized language in the Conclusion claiming REG 'fully unleashes' discriminative potential. None of the findings address rhetorical overstatement or claim scope in the Conclusion; they focus on technical errors and data inconsistencies.

GT 12 concerns Section 4.2 downplaying +0.30% parameter and +0.49% latency overhead as 'negligible' despite potential practical impacts. None of the findings examine computational cost presentation or efficiency claims; all focus on equation errors and data inconsistencies.

GT 13 identifies sensational language in the Abstract title 'Is Much Easier Than You Think' as promotional rather than neutral scientific tone. None of the findings address title framing or rhetorical style; all focus on technical content errors.
